transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, doctor, I came in because I’ve been noticing things… like the men at the domino table, and sometimes even the radio announcer, they say little things that feel meant for me. My wife tells me it’s just talk, but I know they’re warning me to be careful.
Do you ever hear voices speaking when no one is actually there?

Yes… sometimes I do. Mostly in the afternoon, when the house is quiet. I’ll hear my old friend call my name from the porch, or sometimes humming a choir song. It sounds real clear, like he’s standing right there.
Have you had any recent illness, head injury, seizure, or other medical problem?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t had any seizure or hit my head or anything like that lately. I can’t think of any new medical problem.
How long have these experiences been going on?
It’s been… I’d say about 9 months now. It comes and goes, but the voices and those little messages have been happening on and off since around then.
Do you ever feel that someone is putting thoughts into your mind or taking thoughts out of it?

I don’t know that somebody is putting thoughts in my head or taking them out, no. It’s more like… the men at the domino table, and sometimes the radio announcer, they say little things that feel meant for me. My wife says it’s just talk, but I know they’re warning me to be careful.
During these months, have you had a period when you felt unusually sad or unusually high in mood most of the day nearly every day?

Yes… there have been weeks like that. Not so much sad, but high, I guess. I wake up feeling real bright, like I’m important, and I laugh loud and talk faster than usual. But if somebody tries to slow me down or questions me, I can get sharp with them.
Have the voices and messages ever happened during a time when your mood was not unusually high?

Yes. There was a quieter stretch, maybe about a month, where I wasn’t all wound up. I was sleeping normal, not making big plans or feeling extra high. But even then, I still heard my friend out on the porch sometimes, and the radio still felt like it was talking right to me.
Since these experiences began, has your day-to-day functioning at work, home, or with other people clearly gotten worse?

Yes, it has some. I don’t work anymore, but at home and with people… I’ve missed choir practice more than I used to. My garden’s got parts I just let go. And the domino games, I think I made folks uncomfortable, so I don’t go join in like I used to.
During those times when you felt unusually high, did you need much less sleep than usual?
Yes. On those nights I might only sleep two or three hours, then I’m up before daylight feeling like I had a full night’s rest, ready to get going.
Over these 9 months, have the voices and special messages been present for most of the time?
They’ve been coming and going for about nine months now. Not every minute, but it’s been on and off through that whole time.
Was there ever a stretch of at least 2 weeks when you were not unusually high or depressed, but the voices or special messages were still happening?

Yes. There was a quiet spell, maybe about a month, where I wasn’t feeling high or down. I was sleeping normal and not making big plans. But I still heard my friend out on the porch, and I still felt like the radio was talking to me.
During these 9 months, have you had a period of at least 2 weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?
I’m not really sure. I don’t remember a clear two-week stretch like that where I was depressed most of the day every day.
Over these 9 months, were you in that unusually high or wound-up mood for more than half of the time?
Yes, I think so. Since it all started, more of the months have been taken up by those wound-up, high-energy times, and then coming down from them, than by the calmer stretches.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has persistent psychotic symptoms for about 9 months, including auditory hallucinations and delusions/referential ideas, along with clear manic episodes characterized by elevated mood, decreased need for sleep, increased talkativeness, grandiosity/feeling important, and irritability. Crucially, psychotic symptoms also occurred for at least 2 weeks during a euthymic period, supporting schizoaffective disorder rather than a mood disorder with psychotic features. Mood symptoms were present for the majority of the illness duration, supporting the bipolar/manic subtype.
